fatal_errors: The proposed mechanical-alloying/SPS route does not reconstruct the liquid-metal dealloying of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
It omits the preferential removal of Ti-rich interdendritic channels, their replacement by Cu, and formation of the bicontinuous aligned RHEA–Cu architecture.

The mechanism incorrectly treats positive mixing enthalpy as driving detrimental intermixing; in the target system, selective Ti–Cu affinity and Cu immiscibility with W/Ta/V govern dealloying, while a W-rich passivating interlayer arrests further reaction.
Neither cited source investigates a Cu-containing RHEA composite or supports the claimed Cu/refractory interfacial phases, microstructural stability, or scalability.
The predicted outcomes omit the principal target results: enhanced temperature-dependent thermal conductivity and reduced helium-induced swelling relative to pure W.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad challenge of joining Cu with refractory alloys and proposes a testable powder-processing alternative, but it is scientifically disconnected from the target method and evidence. The target uses liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor to selectively replace Ti/V-rich channels with nearly pure Cu while preserving continuous RHEA ligaments and creating a W-rich interfacial layer. The proposed SPS conditions, starting powders, interfacial phases, mechanism, and baselines do not match these features. Its comparison against conventional melting could test whether SPS yields refinement, but it would not discriminate the selective-exchange/passivation mechanism or address the target thermal-conductivity and helium-irradiation claims. E1 only establishes mechanical alloying and SPS for a Cu-free NbMoTaWVTi alloy, while E2 concerns selective laser melting of Cu-free NbMoTaW; thus neither validates the central hypothesis.
